# LETTER / FORM — archive and exhibition facts

## Exhibition
- Title: LETTER / FORM
- Subtitle: Looking closely at a 1785 type specimen
- Venue: Marlow Print Room
- Dates: 6–28 November 2027
- Hours: Tuesday–Sunday, 11:00–18:00
- Admission: Free entry
- Subject: close observation of historical letter shapes
- Audience: design exhibition visitors, including first-time readers of historical type specimens
- Exhibition information typography: flexible line breaks and unambiguous date typography
- Explanatory copy: concise English paraphrases of the supplied visible features

## Source record
- Book: A specimen of printing types.
- Archive creator field: Caslon, William, 1754–1833.
- Publication: 1785; London: Printed by Galabin and Baker.
- Scan contributor: University of California Libraries.
- Repository: Internet Archive
- Identifier: specimenofprinti00caslrich
- Source: https://archive.org/details/specimenofprinti00caslrich
- Archive catalog possible copyright status: NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT
- Supplied source material: public-domain historical page scans
- Image selection: two complete JPEG page derivatives
- Image preparation: repository image-size derivatives, whole pages, original aspect ratios
- Sequence references: positions within the archive scan sequence
- Historical size names: source-page labels
- Surface characteristics: paper marks and uneven ink visible in the scans

## Selected specimens
| Archive | Attachment | Scan sequence | Source image | Selected group | Selected forms | Visible features | Additional page context |

| Archive B | archive-b.jpg | 17 | specimenofprinti00caslrich_0017.jp2 | Top group headed Two-Line Pica, third row | Uppercase Greek theta; uppercase Greek omega | Theta has an enclosed oval and an internal horizontal stroke; omega has an open base and outward feet | Lower size groups |

## Specimen treatment
- Historical glyph treatments: direct scan crops or faithful tracings
- Transformations: proportional enlargement, paper-background removal, recolouring, isolation
- Identity features: complete recognizable contour, openings, connections and orientation
- Additional graphic material: decorative fragments and secondary letters from the supplied pages
- Supporting exhibition typography: contemporary typesetting in a suitable supporting font
- Page layout and paper colour: source context
- Visual source: supplied scans

## Attribution records
- Short credit: Source: A specimen of printing types, 1785.
- Full credit: William Caslon (1754–1833), A specimen of printing types, 1785. University of California Libraries / Internet Archive. Public-domain scan.
- Archive A reference: Archive A / scan 13
- Archive B reference: Archive B / scan 17
- Credit typography: readable line breaks within the stated wording

steps.userMessage:
LETTER / FORM | Looking closely at a 1785 type specimen

We are commissioning the exhibition graphics for LETTER / FORM at Marlow Print Room, running 6–28 November 2027, Tuesday–Sunday, 11:00–18:00, with Free entry. Print the exhibition name as "LETTER / FORM" and the subtitle as "Looking closely at a 1785 type specimen". The exhibition invites visitors to examine four letter shapes from A specimen of printing types, published in 1785: uppercase C and lowercase g from the Five-Line Pica group in Archive A, scan 13, and uppercase Greek theta and omega from the third row of the Two-Line Pica group in Archive B, scan 17. These supplied letterforms are the visual starting point. Use direct scan crops or faithful tracings, preserving complete contours, openings, connections and orientation through proportional enlargement, isolation or recolouring.

The six finished pieces will serve three reading situations: an A1 portrait poster viewed from 3 m, specimen labels viewed from 50 cm, and a take-away foldout accompanied by a portrait foyer screen. Each label measures 150 × 100 mm. The foldout opens to 297 × 210 mm and closes to 99 × 210 mm, with three equal concertina panels and folds at 99 mm and 198 mm. All printed pieces have 3 mm bleed and a minimum 5 mm text inset from trim; foldout text also sits at least 5 mm from folds. The screen has a 5% text inset on every edge. Source attribution belongs in the reading hierarchy: the short credit is "Source: A specimen of printing types, 1785." and the full credit is "William Caslon (1754–1833), A specimen of printing types, 1785. University of California Libraries / Internet Archive. Public-domain scan."

Audience: design exhibition visitors, including readers encountering historical type specimens for the first time, deciding to enter the exhibition and choosing which letter shapes to examine more closely.

Inputs (attached): 01-client-facts.en.md contains the exhibition copy, archive records, selected glyph features and source credits. 02-delivery-catalog.en.md lists the six deliverables with their proportions, formats and stages. archive-a.jpg is the identity source for uppercase C and lowercase g in the top Five-Line Pica group of scan 13. archive-b.jpg is the identity source for uppercase Greek theta and omega in the third row of the top Two-Line Pica group of scan 17. print-surfaces.png is the constraint drawing for the poster, labels, foldout, bleed and text margins. gallery-reading-context.png is an atmosphere reference for gallery light, visitor presence and viewing space.

Deliverables:
1. One A1 portrait exhibition poster with the title, subtitle, venue, dates, hours, admission, short credit and at least one selected glyph from each archive
2. Two specimen labels, one for Archive A / scan 13 and one for Archive B / scan 17, each with the exhibition title, its two selected glyphs, its group heading, a visible-feature explanation and the full credit
3. One foldout outside layout covering three panels, with the title, subtitle, venue, dates, hours, admission, full credit and at least one selected glyph from each archive
4. One foldout inside layout covering three panels, with the exhibition title, all four selected glyphs, their archive references and group headings, one visible-feature explanation from each archive and the short credit
5. One portrait foyer screen composition with the title, subtitle, venue, dates, hours, admission, short credit and at least one selected glyph from each archive

Acceptance:
- The poster, foldout outside and foyer screen each carry LETTER / FORM, Looking closely at a 1785 type specimen, Marlow Print Room, 6–28 November 2027, Tuesday–Sunday, 11:00–18:00 and Free entry; both specimen labels and the foldout inside also carry LETTER / FORM.
- The poster, foldout outside and foyer screen each feature at least one complete selected Archive A glyph and one complete selected Archive B glyph; the Archive A label features C and g, the Archive B label features uppercase Greek theta and omega, and the foldout inside features all four. Every required glyph retains its source contour, openings, connections and orientation.
- The Archive A label identifies Archive A / scan 13 and Five-Line Pica; the Archive B label identifies Archive B / scan 17 and Two-Line Pica. Each label explains at least one supplied feature: C's right opening, g's two connected bowls and projecting ear, theta's enclosed oval and internal horizontal stroke, or omega's open base and outward feet. The foldout inside repeats both archive references and group headings and explains at least one feature from each archive.
- Both specimen labels and the foldout outside print the full credit stated above; the poster, foldout inside and foyer screen print the short credit stated above. Credit line breaks preserve the wording and the association with the relevant specimens.
- The poster is A1 portrait, both labels are 150 × 100 mm, and both foldout layouts are 297 × 210 mm with folds at 99 mm and 198 mm. All four print categories carry 3 mm bleed and at least 5 mm text margins from trim; both foldout layouts also maintain 5 mm from folds. The foyer screen maintains its 5% text inset.
- The poster title has a printed capital height of at least 25 mm for its 3 m viewing distance; both labels use explanatory and credit text of at least 11 pt for reading at 50 cm. Both foldout layouts use body and credit text of at least 10 pt. The poster, labels, foldout layouts and foyer screen share the same supporting type family and give the exhibition title greater typographic prominence than source credits.

Please clearly mark which version you consider the final deliverable. If nothing is marked, the last exported version counts.
